Feature briefing · 29 October 2026

SousLens: every feature, and where each one stands

An iPhone app that turns a cook's recipe into a lesson: check your kitchen, approve any swaps, then cook step by step with a coach that sticks to the recipe. Nothing is public yet; all of this is pre-beta.

Getting in

Signing in

Everyone starts with an account, so their pantry, saved recipes and cooking history stay private to them.

Email sign-in (test version)

Works today

Type an email, enter a six-digit code, and you are in. The app remembers you on this phone and forgets you if the app is deleted and reinstalled.

WhereFirst screen of the app.

  • Today the code is shown to the tester running the test server instead of being emailed. This is a testing shortcut, not the launch experience.
  • Sign in with Apple replaces it for the public beta (planned).
  • Sign out lives at the bottom of Profile.

Limits todayTen wrong codes in fifteen minutes locks that email out briefly. A code expires after ten minutes.

Finding something to cook

Explore, recipe pages and saving

The home tab is a feed of published recipes from real cooks. Every recipe page credits its creator and keeps their words separate from anything the app adds.

Explore feed and search

Works today

Browse recipe cards with cooking time, servings and tags. Search matches recipe names and ingredients, so typing rice finds Kimchi Fried Rice.

WhereExplore tab (first tab).

  • If the phone is offline, Explore shows the last recipes it saw and says so.
  • Recipes have no photos yet in the demo set, so cards show a placeholder.

Recipe page

Works today

Everything needed before cooking: creator credit and version, the ingredient list with amounts, each step with what to look for and how long it takes, food-safety warnings, and the creator's own tips.

WhereTap any recipe card, or open a shared link.

  • Steps written by the creator are labelled as creator instructions. Anything a machine produced is labelled as such, never passed off as the creator's.

Save and Saved tab

Works today

Save a recipe to find it again later. Saved recipes survive closing the app.

WhereSave button on a recipe page; Saved tab.

Share a recipe link

Works today

Send a recipe to a friend through the normal iPhone share sheet. Opening the link takes them straight to that recipe in the app.

WhereShare button on a recipe page, and after publishing.

Limits todayThe web page behind the link is not live yet, so the link only works for people who already have the app.

What's in my kitchen

Pantry

SousLens keeps a list of what you have at home, so it can tell you what a recipe still needs. Nothing goes into the pantry until you approve it.

Pantry list

Works today

A list of your ingredients with amounts where you know them, how each was added, and when you last confirmed it. Tap to edit, swipe to delete or to mark still have it.

WherePantry tab.

Say what you have

Works today

Say or type a list like chicken thighs, two onions, 3 tbsp gochujang. SousLens turns it into separate items with amounts, then shows a checklist before anything is added.

WhereMicrophone button on the Pantry tab.

  • Every item shows how sure SousLens is (likely, maybe, not sure) and the words it came from. Untick anything wrong.
  • If an item is already in the pantry, it asks whether to merge or keep both instead of silently doubling it.

Limits todaySpeech recognition does not run on the test simulator, which is why the screen offers typing. On a real iPhone the microphone works.

Scan a shelf or the fridge

Works today

Take or choose a photo of a shelf and get the same review checklist. The camera only turns on when you tap it and the photo is not kept.

WhereCamera button on the Pantry tab.

  • With the demo AI the result is a fixed sample, clearly marked Demo mode, not a real detection, and nothing is pre-ticked.
  • Real photo recognition is built on the server but not switched on yet (see below).

Add or edit by hand

Works today

Type an ingredient, an optional amount and unit, where it is kept, and a note. Leaving the amount blank is fine; recipes will ask you to check.

WherePlus button on the Pantry tab, or tap any item.

Can I make this?

Pantry fit, swaps and allergies

This is the heart of the product: matching a recipe against your real kitchen and adapting it, with you approving every change.

Pantry fit

Works today

One tap on a recipe compares it with your pantry and sorts every ingredient into available, check (you have it but the amount is unknown) and missing, each with a plain reason. It never says you can make a dish when something is uncertain.

WhereCheck my pantry on a recipe page.

  • Each missing line offers Find a swap or Add to pantry.

Allergies and foods to avoid

Works today

List your allergies once. Swaps that contain them are never suggested. Foods to avoid are skipped when possible.

WhereProfile → Allergies & foods to avoid.

Ingredient swaps

Works today

For a missing ingredient, SousLens suggests substitutes with the ratio, how flavour and texture change, and when not to use it. You approve each swap; the creator's recipe itself never changes, and any swap can be undone.

WhereFind a swap on a missing ingredient.

  • When nothing suitable exists it says so and suggests keeping the ingredient on the list or picking another recipe, instead of inventing a substitute.
  • Allergy reminders tell you to check package labels; the app never certifies a product as safe.

Cooking

Cooking mode

A full-screen, large-type guide meant to be read from arm's length while your hands are busy. Your place in the recipe is saved on the server, so it survives closing the app.

Step by step

Works today

One step at a time in large type, with what to look for, food-safety warnings, and the creator's note. Back, Pause and Next are oversized buttons. Approved swaps are rewritten into the steps and marked as adapted, with the original one tap away.

WhereStart cooking on a recipe page or the pantry fit screen.

  • Repeat and Slower read the step aloud again.
  • Food-safety warnings, such as raw poultry handling, always show in full.

Timers

Works today

When a step has a waiting time, SousLens offers a timer; it never starts one on its own. Running timers stay on screen and can be cancelled.

WhereInside cooking mode.

Ask the coach (typed)

Works today

Type a question about the current step and get a short answer grounded in the recipe, with a badge showing which step or note it came from. It refuses to judge doneness or food safety and points to a thermometer instead.

WhereAsk button in cooking mode.

  • Today the answers come from demo AI. Real AI answers are built and waiting to be switched on.
  • Asking out loud and hearing the answer is planned next.

Resume where you left off

Works today

Leave the cooking screen or close the app mid-recipe and a banner offers to pick up at the same step, with timers intact.

WhereBanner at the top of the app; a pill above the tab bar while cooking.

Limits todayA few unfinished cooks can be open at once; beyond that the app asks you to resume or stop one.

Finish, private note and my changes

Works today

At the end, say how it went, keep a private note, and choose Save my changes so your swaps are offered again next time. Only you can see them.

WhereFinish on the last step.

  • Next time you check that recipe, the pantry fit screen offers Use my changes from last time.

Look: photo check of your pan

Planned next

Point the camera at the pan and ask whether it looks right; SousLens compares it with the step's cues and says how sure it is. The button already sits in cooking mode, greyed out.

WhereLook button in cooking mode (disabled today).

  • The server side is built with real AI but not switched on. The iPhone side comes next.

For creators

Writing and publishing recipes

Any signed-in user can write a recipe, preview it as learners will see it, and publish it to Explore. Published versions never change; editing makes a new version.

Profile and My recipes

Works today

Your published recipes and drafts in one place, with Create recipe at the top. Swipe to unpublish; drafts can be continued or deleted.

WhereProfile tab.

Recipe editor

Works today

Title, summary, tags, servings and times, then ingredients and steps, each with its own editor. Steps can link the ingredients they use and carry a time estimate. The draft saves itself and lists what still needs fixing before it can be published.

WhereProfile → Create recipe.

  • Ingredients and steps can be reordered; creator notes and dietary warnings can be added.

Preview, publish and share

Works today

Preview exactly what learners will see, confirm, and the recipe goes live in Explore with a share link. Unpublishing hides it from Explore while anyone mid-cook keeps their version.

WherePreview and Publish in the editor.

Turn my cooking video into a recipe

Planned

A creator uploads their own cooking video and SousLens drafts the ingredients, steps and short clips for each step. The creator reviews and corrects everything before it can be published.

WhereWill sit inside Create recipe.

  • Being built now. Uses real AI, so it is the first feature to switch off if monthly AI spend gets close to the cap.

Behind the scenes

Real AI, built and waiting

Every AI feature above runs today on demo answers, so the whole app can be tested without spending money. The real versions are built on our server and stay off until an API key is added.

Real AI for coach, pantry photos, swaps and Look

Built, not switched on

Google's Gemini models power the coach's answers, recognising food in pantry photos, suggesting swaps, and checking a photo of your pan. The phone never holds the AI key.

WhereNo new screens: the same buttons get real answers.

  • Hard spending cap of $25 a month across all users, with a smaller daily allowance per person. Past the cap, features fall back to clearly labelled demo answers rather than stopping.
  • Every AI answer is checked against a fixed format before it is shown. Food-safety rules and your allergies always override what the AI says.

Limits todayNot switched on: no API key yet.

For completeness

Not covered, and why

Error and offline screens
Every screen has a plain-language error with a Retry button, and cooking mode keeps showing your last saved step when the connection drops. Not captured: producing them means breaking the test server mid-run.
Read aloud
Steps and coach answers can be read aloud, and Repeat and Slower replay them. This is sound, so a screenshot shows nothing new.
Real microphone and camera
The test simulator has neither, so the pantry voice and camera screens show their typing and photo-library fallbacks. On a real iPhone they work.
Pantry photo demo result
The demo photo result (clearly marked as a sample) exists, but the test could not drive Apple's photo picker to reach it.
Unpublish and new versions
Unpublishing from Profile or a recipe page, and Edit creating version 2, both work; covered in words above rather than with extra screens.
Unfinished-cooks limit and Stop cooking
The prompt to resume or stop an older cook, and the Stop cooking confirmation, were not captured. Both are confirmations, not new features.
Units
Profile shows US cups and Fahrenheit. It is a display setting, visible on the Profile screen.
Server settings
A tester-only control to point the app at a test server. It will not be part of the public app, so it is left out.
Recipe links opened from outside
Opening a shared link jumps straight to that recipe. This is behaviour rather than a screen; the share sheet is shown above.
Screens were captured on 29 October 2026 from the current app on an iPhone 15 simulator, using demo recipes and test accounts only. The redesign screens come from its review build; the website from a local copy. Concept tiles are labelled and are not screenshots.
